name: Human drums on any step sequencer: four-on-the-floor kick, eighth hats with the hats that land on the kick turned down, 56% swing, a 16th-hat layer only on the second bar with every other hit softer, open hat on the last step of bar 2, a loose clap built from 3-4 stacked clap tracks nudged early/late with varied velocity and pitch, a track with an odd 24-step second bar and an 8-bar reset, random sample-start drift on the closed hat, and a pumping bus compressor
goal: Get movement and feel into rigid step-sequenced drums with velocity, micro-timing and pattern length rather than more parts: accent the off-beat hats, add a second-bar 16th hat layer, build a loose 'flammed' clap from stacked copies shifted slightly early and late, let one track's pattern length make a cycle against the bar, and glue with a pumping compressor. Delta vs our groove variants: four-on-the-floor velocity shaping, stacked-clap flam and odd-length pattern resets.

source.title: Drum programming Tips for ANY machine

prerequisites: Any step sequencer or drum machine with per-step velocity, swing, micro-timing, per-track length and an LFO
Kick, closed/open hat and clap sounds (synthesized or own samples)

outputs.name: groove
outputs.description: 2-bar (and 8-bar cycle) drum groove with human feel

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Keep the kick on the grid; feel comes from hats and claps.
Micro-timing offsets are small and fixed per copy (no random pitch).
Bring the drums in early (by about count 8).
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Eighth hats: lower the velocity of the hats that coincide with the kick so the off-beat hats stand out; set swing to about 56%.
steps.expect: Bouncy hat line that sounds compressed

steps.action: On a second hat track, add 16th hats only in the second bar of a two-bar pattern, with every other hit lower in velocity.
Put a softer, slightly pitched-down open hat on step 15 of bar 2 with a little reverb send.

Loose clap: copy the clap to 3-4 tracks; leave one on the grid, push one a little early, one later and one even later; vary velocities and pitch one copy up (and one far down, quieter, high-passed); add a little reverb.
Make one track 32 steps with the second bar shortened to 24 steps and a pattern reset every 8 bars (128 steps), so it cycles against the bar.
On the closed hat, route a slow, free LFO (odd length) at low depth to sample start, with a soft attack.
Balance the claps down, then add a pumping bus compressor; if the kick blooms too much, shorten it and tune it down slightly.

verification: Kick-aligned hats are measurably lower in velocity than off-beat hats.
Clap copies are offset by small, different amounts.
Pattern repeats exactly only every 8 bars.
